criteria.criterion: In studies/firstmate-work-handling/model.json the places-held counter's changed_by lists every transition that frees or takes a place (spawn t1, the ready-PR report t3, and cleanup t4), matching claim c3 and t2's retry.changes 'falls when another worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up'; the file no longer contradicts itself.
criteria.evidence: I read model.json. Line 12 is changed_by ["t1","t3","t4"]. t1 is the spawn, t3 is in-flight→ready (the worker reports a PR), and t4 is the teardown to done. t2's retry.changes (line 29) and claim c3 in claims.json say the same thing. The unit test the_shipped_firstmate_model_is_consistent passes.

criteria.criterion: No page text in intro.json says a place is freed by anything other than a recorded PR or a cleanup; each such sentence cites c3.
criteria.evidence: I searched intro.json for free/place/slot. Only two sentences say how a place is freed: the counters leadin (line 30) and the places-held glossary entry (line 55). Both say 'only when a worker records its ready PR or is cleaned up', and both cite ["c3"]. No other text gives a different way to free a place.

criteria.criterion: Drain no longer reports Stop::TargetMet from a rating at or above the target alone: it also requires a passing check of the page against the pinned source. A test in crates/athena-cli/tests/drain.rs shows a 4 rating with a failing check does not stop drain, and a 4 rating with a passing check does. Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`.
criteria.evidence: In drain.rs, met_target = rated_enough && check_page().passed. In tests/drain.rs, a_rating_at_the_target_stops_drain_only_with_a_passing_source_check covers both cases: with a passing check, a 4 gives TargetMet after the first landing; with a failing check, two 4s give QueueEmpty with 2 landed. That test and a_rating_below_the_target_does_not_ask_for_the_source_check passed. tests/drain.rs: 20 passed, 0 failed.

criteria.criterion: A test shows the check fails on the earlier contradiction (a counter's changed_by omitting a transition whose retry changes it). Run `cargo test`.
criteria.evidence: The unit test drain::tests::a_counter_whose_changed_by_omits_a_transition_its_retry_changes_is_a_contradiction uses changed_by [t1,t3] with t2's real retry text. It expects one contradiction naming places-held and t2, and none once t4 is added. It passed, and the whole workspace run had 0 failures. I ran `cargo test -q`, which is `cargo test` with only quieter output.

criteria.criterion: The drain report says which check held drain back when it keeps running. Run `cargo test`; `cargo clippy` is clean and `cargo fmt --check` passes.
criteria.evidence: display.rs prints the rating line as 'target not met: held back by the source check' and adds a 'held back … : {why}' line. The integration test checks that the text contains 'held back' and the finding, and does not contain 'target met'. All tests passed, clippy gave no warnings with -D warnings, and cargo fmt --check printed nothing (exit 0).

findings.summary: The user-facing text calls this a check 'of the page against the pinned source', but it only checks that the study models agree with themselves.
findings.evidence: model_contradictions reads only model.json. It reads no source and no page. CHANGELOG and D99 say so honestly ('a floor… does not read the source'), but the report and the stop meaning promise more than the check does.
findings.location: crates/athena-cli/src/display.rs (held back line); crates/athena-cli/src/drain.rs Stop::TargetMet meaning

findings.summary: The check is fragile: it counts the ways a place is freed by splitting the retry text on " or ", and it matches a counter by substring.
findings.evidence: needed = 1 + text.split(" or ").count(), and the counter is matched with text.contains(id). Other wording would be missed, or would cause false failures, and a false failure would keep drain running. Accepted as a tradeoff in D99.

findings.summary: No test covers RealSteps::check_page, the code that reads studies/*/model.json at the head commit.
findings.evidence: The integration tests use a stub check_page, and the unit tests call model_contradictions directly. Nothing tests the ls_tree_under and show_file path or its fail-closed error branch.

summary: The change does what was asked. In model.json, places-held now lists t1, t3 and t4, which matches claim c3 and t2's retry text. intro.json now says a place is freed only by a recorded PR or a cleanup, and both sentences that say so cite c3. Drain now ends on "target met" only when the rating is high enough and a new check, Steps::check_page, also passes. The real check is model_contradictions, which runs no model and reads each studies/*/model.json at the head commit. When the check fails, the rating line and a "held back" line in the report say what it found. The drain tests cover both cases (a 4 with a failing check keeps drain running; a 4 with a passing check stops it). A unit test shows the check fails on the old changed_by list, and another shows the shipped model passes. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli`, `cargo test`, `cargo clippy --all-targets --locked -- -D warnings` and `cargo fmt --check` in this snapshot, and all passed. Every changed file is on the deliverables list. My findings are minor: the report calls this a check "against the pinned source", but it only checks that the model agrees with itself. The way it counts the ways a place is freed is fragile. And no test drives RealSteps::check_page itself.
